Vendored mojito-sys S6.3/S6.4/S6.6 readiness substrate —
mojito_async/vendor/mojito-sys/{mjs_poller.c,mjs_epoll.c,mjs_iouring.c,
include/mojito_sys.h}

Source repository: github.com/mojito-async/mojito-sys
Source tree:       native/posix/{mjs_poller.c,mjs_epoll.c,mjs_iouring.c},
                    native/include/mojito_sys.h
Source commit:      48b4f8fd7bc04aba1ca8d8e4a20c7ec315482619 (main)
Vendored on:        2026-08-30 (re-vendor of mjs_iouring.c ONLY, issue #168)

RE-VENDOR 2026-08-30 (issue #168). mjs_iouring.c was refreshed from
upstream `main` to pick up two fixes it predated; the other three files in
this slice were already byte-identical to the new commit and did not
change. mojito_sys.h in particular is UNCHANGED, so nothing here touches
the frozen ABI and this re-vendor does not intersect mojito-sys#164.

  mojito-sys#167  ioring_enter returns the NUMBER OF SQES CONSUMED.
                  uring_submit_poll_add passed that through while its
                  docstring promised "0 or negative errno", and
                  mjs_iouring_create/register tested it with `!= 0`. So
                  create armed its wake poll, read the 1 SQE back as a
                  failure, tore down the ring it had just built and
                  returned +1. The backend's only success configuration
                  was unreachable, and create_completion_poller() raised
                  a fabricated "POSIX errno 1" on every Linux host with
                  the flag set.
  mojito-sys#169  iouring_unmap recomputed each mapping's length from a
                  different formula than iouring_map_rings used, so at
                  4 KiB pages sq_ring was unmapped a page short and
                  cq_ring two pages long, silently releasing whatever
                  followed the cq ring. The two map-failure paths also
                  released nothing at all, because they ran before the
                  entry counts those formulas needed were assigned. Each
                  mapping's exact mmap length is now stored beside its
                  pointer and unmapped verbatim.

Verified after copying by building THIS vendored file as a Linux shared
object on a native aarch64 kernel and running mojito-sys's own s6 drivers
against it (tests/s6/iouring_submit for #167, tests/s6/iouring_unmap for
#169). Both report all green; before the copy the same drivers reported
RED against this file.

FILES (byte-identical to upstream `main` at the commit above; fetched via
`gh api repos/mojito-async/mojito-sys/contents/<path>` with the raw
media-type accept header, diff -r against a fresh clone is empty):
  include/mojito_sys.h   # the FULL frozen native ABI header (S1-S6 blocks:
                          #   ctx/stack, thread/TLS, mutex/sem/condvar,
                          #   atomic-wait, event, socket, s6-poller/epoll/
                          #   ioring).  Vendored WHOLE (not trimmed) so this
                          #   header stays the single canonical copy other
                          #   A7 lanes (#77/#78 socket, future epoll/
                          #   io_uring work) can #include without a second,
                          #   possibly-divergent partial header appearing
                          #   under this same vendor tree.
  mjs_poller.c            # s6-poller: kqueue readiness backend (issue #75).
                          #   Darwin/BSD: real kqueue implementation.  Every
                          #   other host: detect-and-exclude stub returning
                          #   exactly -ENOSYS from every entry point (no
                          #   #ifdef needed at the call site).
  mjs_epoll.c              # s6-epoll: Linux epoll readiness backend.  Same
                          #   detect-and-exclude discipline; -ENOSYS stub on
                          #   this (Darwin) build host — untested on Linux
                          #   by this lane, exercised by mjs_poller.c's twin
                          #   kqueue path instead.  Vendored so
                          #   reactor/poller.mojo's platform pick has a real
                          #   epoll target to compile against once a Linux
                          #   CI host runs this suite (spec §27.1/§28).
  mjs_iouring.c            # s6-ioring: EXPERIMENTAL completion backend
                          #   behind the MOJITO_IO_URING=1 capability flag
                          #   (ADR-SYS-009).  Linux-only; -ENOSYS stub here.
                          #   reactor/poller.mojo's create_completion_poller
                          #   binds to this and is exercised only via its
                          #   guaranteed--ENOSYS-on-this-host path (the
                          #   acceptance criterion "completion backend is
                          #   unreachable without the flag").

Nothing else from native/posix/ or native/include/ was pulled: mjs_socket.c
(NativeSocket/connect/accept, issues #77/#78) is a SEPARATE vendoring slice
owned by the A7 connect/accept lane, layered on the SAME
include/mojito_sys.h above (do not vendor a second copy of the header).

The Makefile's `mojito_async/vendor/mojito-sys/*.c`/`*.S` wildcard picks
these up automatically (see repo-root Makefile header comment); no
Makefile edit was needed. Verified: `make` links libmojito_spike.dylib
with mjs_poller.o/mjs_epoll.o/mjs_iouring.o alongside the pre-existing S0
(ms_ctx/native_stack/aarch64_switch), S2 (cpu_count) and E6 (ms_event)
objects with zero symbol/header conflicts (disjoint `mjs_`/`ms_`
extern-prefix families, disjoint #include sets).
